summary.headline: Kalyani Forge FY26 PAT rose to Rs 9.32 crore, highest in about 14 years, with Q4 EBITDA margin at 15.2%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue flat at about Rs 238 crore as roughly Rs 40 crore of non-fit business was phased out, while EBITDA rose to Rs 31.58 crore (13.3% margin) from Rs 26 crore (11.1%). Q4 EBITDA was about Rs 9 crore at 15.2% margin, the second consecutive quarter above 15%. Q4 PAT of Rs 5.88 crore was helped by a reversal of deferred tax after a near-zero Q3 PAT. Management said 15% is now a floor and targets about 20% EBITDA margin within a year.

segments.name: Engine (incl. connecting rods)
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue; core business mainly for HCV, off-road and agro applications, with long-term visibility per management.

segments.name: Driveline
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue; described as fast-growing, mainly passenger cars, and fuel-agnostic including EVs. Sales at highest level in last four to five quarters.

segments.name: Axle
segments.commentary: About 10% of revenue; fast-growing and fuel-agnostic. New EV high-volume axle order worth Rs 20 crore annual revenue won.

segments.name: OEM revenue
segments.commentary: Rs 37.3 crore in FY26, highest in several quarters over almost two years, per management.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20% EBITDA margin, expected within about a year, moving closer to 20% by end FY27 or early FY28.
FY27 focus: profitable growth, cash conversion cycle reduction, ROCE improvement and sustaining 15%+ EBITDA margin.
Cash conversion cycle target at first level of 120 to 130 days, from a peak of 176 days in Q2 FY26.
Debt-to-equity target of about 1.2 to 1.2 (management said 1.2 to 1); equity funding being prepared.
FY27 capex plan of Rs 30 crore: existing Rs 5 crore, ramp-up Rs 10 crore, new business Rs 10 crore, future Rs 5 crore; 60% to growth areas.
Management indicated steady-state revenue of about Rs 300 crore on Rs 90-99 crore fixed assets at asset turnover of about 3x.
capex_capacity: PPE installed Rs 86.5 crore vs Rs 60.5 crore last year; CWIP Rs 10.3 crore.
FY26 capex Rs 23.44 crore excluding reclassification; Rs 10 crore of dies and toolings reclassified from inventory to fixed assets.
Fixed asset turnover declining toward the industry benchmark of 1.5 to 2; company has historically run at 3.5 to 4x.
Capex budgets now tied to core customer programs at granular level; machine reconditioning and die-run prioritisation improving uptime.
Plant Engineering vertical started in Q4 FY26 to redesign layouts, pipelines and electrical circuits; management says it needs little capex.
demand_pricing: Three major order wins in Q4, including OEM wheel hubs from SKF and Schaeffler, ramping from Q1 FY27.
New EV high-volume axle order worth Rs 20 crore annual revenue; Gen 3 passenger car hubs cited.
Phased out about Rs 40 crore of non-fit, low-margin, low-volume export and legacy business in FY26; exports were 11% of sales in Q4.
Additional business allocated by top customers on core engine business; management claims it is the only forging company offering engine, driveline and axle components to OEMs.
Order book for new business unchanged vs Q3 as some items moved into production; programs typically 5 to 10 years, some over 20 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 interest cost only Rs 0.24 crore when borrowings have increased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said term-loan interest from earlier quarters was capitalised in Q4 as significant capex was installed, so the full-year interest cost should be looked at instead.

qa_highlights.question: What maximum sales can the current fixed asset base support?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at a fixed asset turnover of about 3x on Rs 90-99 crore of fixed assets, steady-state revenue would be about Rs 300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising faster than sales and what is the right cash conversion cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer credit controls and safety-stock or warehousing commitments to some key OEMs; target is 120 to 130 days CCC at first level.

qa_highlights.question: How will EBITDA margin trend from the 15% base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% is now a floor; target is 20% within about a year, driven by OEM mix, pricing and cost programmes.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the other income is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other income includes export and government incentives, which are stable and will grow with exports, plus routine sale of obsolete assets; part is recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new business order book unchanged from Q3 and are these multi-year programs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is unchanged because some items moved to production; all programs are multi-year, typically 5 to 10 years.

risks_watch: Receivables and working capital stretch from OEM safety-stock commitments; CCC progress vs 120 to 130 day target.
Q4 PAT boosted by deferred-tax reversal and capitalisation timing; quarterly PAT volatility expected to continue.
Interest cost of Rs 0.24 crore in Q4 looks low because of capitalisation; watch whether it normalises.
Debt-to-equity at 1.11 and rising; equity fundraise still in preparation with no timeline given.
Other income (incentives and asset sales) of about Rs 2 crore higher YoY is partly non-recurring; quality of earnings.
Clean audit roadmap in Phase 2 with external consultant; governance remediation ongoing.
Revenue flat YoY; growth depends on ramp-up of SKF and Schaeffler wheel hub orders from Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and margin floor, but cautious on working capital and debt, which management acknowledged as areas of focus. Answers on finance cost and other income were somewhat accounting-heavy and partly deflected to full-year figures. Forward targets (20% margin, 120-130 day CCC) were stated without a detailed bridge.
key_quotes: 15% is now a floor, it's a baseline. And it's a minimum that we need to be achieving.
Going forward, we are targeting 20% EBITDA margin, which we hope to reach, I'd say, in a year's time.
We have a PPE installed of Rs. 86.5 crores now, versus Rs. 60.5 crores last year, a CWIP of 10.3 crores.
We have always operated at a level of 3.5 to 4 which is highly stretched.

growth.why: Management guides to profitable growth and a 20% EBITDA margin within about a year, with FY26 revenue flat at about Rs 238 crore after Rs 40 crore of non-fit business was phased out; backing is partial, with three Q4 OEM wins (SKF, Schaeffler, EV axle worth Rs 20 crore annual revenue) and a Rs 30 crore FY27 capex plan, but no specific new capacity count or timeline and no revenue growth guidance g

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: within about a year (FY27 end / early FY28)
rows.why: Management says 15% EBITDA margin is now a floor, with Q4 at 15.2% (second straight quarter above 15%) and FY26 at 13.3% vs 11.1%, and targets 20% driven by OEM mix, pricing and cost programmes, though no detailed bridge was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rs 30 crore FY27 capex plan (Rs 5 cr existing, Rs 10 cr ramp-up, Rs 10 cr new business, Rs 5 cr future) but no specific new plant, line or capacity count was named, and PPE rose to Rs 86.5 crore from Rs 60.5 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H1 FY27, ramping from Q1 FY27
rows.why: Three Q4 OEM wins (SKF and Schaeffler wheel hubs ramping from Q1 FY27, plus an EV axle order worth Rs 20 crore annual revenue) follow FY26 revenue that was flat at about Rs 238 crore after Rs 40 crore of non-fit business was phased out.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fixed asset turnover is falling toward 1.5-2x from a historical 3.5-4x and management ties capex to core programmes, but utilisation was not quantified (only 'increasing output and capacity utilization'), so a new capex announcement is conditional rather than firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on profitability, with ROCE up to 18% in Q4 from 14% in Q1 FY26, but gave no revenue growth guidance, so an upgrade depends on the SKF/Schaeffler ramp showing up in revenue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cash conversion cycle is at 176 days peak in Q2 FY26 against a 120-130 day target, debt-to-equity is 1.11 and rising, and Q4 PAT was flattered by a deferred-tax reversal and low Q4 interest cost of Rs 0.24 crore from capitalisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New EV high-volume axle order worth Rs 20 crore annual revenue and Gen 3 passenger car hubs cited, with Driveline and Axle described as fast-growing and fuel-agnostic (Axle about 10% of revenue).

rows.label: Cash conversion cycle to 120-130 days
rows.why: CCC peaked at 176 days in Q2 FY26 and management is targeting 120-130 days, but the receivables stretch from OEM safety-stock commitments is ongoing and no timeline was given.

rows.label: Equity raise to bring debt-to-equity to about 1.2
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is 1.11 and rising on growth capex and working capital, and management says equity funding is being prepared without a date.

rows.label: Multi-year OEM programme wins
rows.why: Programmes run 5 to 10 years, some over 20, and the new-business order book was flat vs Q3 at some items moving into production.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15% margin floor, the 20% target and the SKF/Schaeffler ramp, but cautious on working capital and debt; analysts pressed on the low Q4 interest cost, other income quality and receivables, and answers leaned on full-year figures and capitalisation accounting.
